DESCRIPTION:  
FIND: Allocation-degradation telemetry is wired to the wrong owner, so the Experiment 17 immune/load-balancing trace cannot actually observe `LoadBalancer` warnings. `LoadBalancer` owns `_allocation_warnings` at [dynamic_management.py#L857](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L857) and appends to it in `_solve_greedy()` at [dynamic_management.py#L1059](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1059) and [dynamic_management.py#L1076](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1076). But `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` creates a local `LoadBalancer` and immediately discards it at [dynamic_management.py#L5272](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5272) and [dynamic_management.py#L5278](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5278). Later, telemetry reads `getattr(mgr, '_allocation_warnings', [])` from the manager at [run_exp17_immune.py#L1411](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1411) and [run_exp17_immune.py#L1412](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp17_immune.py#L1412), even though that field is never populated on `DynamicManager`. The runtime evidence matches the code path: [telemetry.json#L25](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/logs/experiment_17/telemetry.json#L25), [telemetry.json#L94](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/logs/experiment_17/telemetry.json#L94), [telemetry.json#L193](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/logs/experiment_17/telemetry.json#L193), and [telemetry.json#L304](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/logs/experiment_17/telemetry.json#L304) all record `"allocation_warnings": []`. This is a false-negative observability defect at the LoadBalancer → DynamicManager → immune telemetry boundary.

FIX:  
<<<< old
        lb = LoadBalancer(
            active_models,
            tasks,
            self.role_assignment.role_map,

        return lb.solve()
====

        lb = LoadBalancer(
            active_models,
            tasks,
            self.role_assignment.role_map,
            self.config,
        )
        allocation, cost, is_balanced = lb.solve()
        self._allocation_warnings = list(lb._allocation_warnings)
        return allocation, cost, is_balanced
>>>>

<<<< old
    # Allocation warnings (LoadBalancer is constructed locally in DM, not stored)
    warnings = getattr(mgr, '_allocation_warnings', [])
====
    # Allocation warnings captured from the most recent DynamicManager.get_allocation() call
    warnings = list(getattr(mgr, '_allocation_warnings', []))
>>>>

FOLLOW: This fix makes allocation degradation visible, but it also reveals a round-scoping assumption. If any path records telemetry without calling `get_allocation()` first, the manager-side cache could be stale from a prior round. The robust long-term follow-on is to carry `allocation_warnings` on a round-scoped result object instead of a manager cache. Within the shown Exp17 path, no other immune component reads `_allocation_warnings`, so no additional behavioral regression is introduced by this change.

PROPOSED_FIX: Persist the latest `LoadBalancer._allocation_warnings` onto `DynamicManager` inside `get_allocation()`, and have telemetry read that copied list rather than a nonexistent manager field.
